rawCommits.subject: feat(marketing): mock projects desktop on /code page
rawCommits.body:
Restructure the /code page to lead with an Agents-style centered
PageHero, then a mock desktop below it. The desktop reuses the shared
MockAuraApp chrome (titlebar + taskbar + wallpaper) with a new
optional centerContent prop, swapping the landing's scripted DM
windows for a static MockProjectsWorkspace that mocks the app's
Projects workspace (explorer + agent status + task feed + terminal +
sidekick). Layout-only pass; copy and workspace content are
placeholders to refine next.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: mock projects desktop on /code page

rawCommits.subject: fix(channels): pin model for telegram turns and surface agent errors
rawCommits.body:
Telegram-linked agent turns POSTed model: null, so agents without a
default_model failed the harness turn with "model name must not be
empty" and the user only saw a generic apology. The picker-less external
chat surface now pins the latest frontier model at medium reasoning
effort for every turn.

Also thread agent-reported errors back to the chat via a new
ChannelError::Agent variant instead of collapsing every failure into the
generic message, and greet the user with the agent's real name
("Connected to <name>") by carrying the name through the pending and
durable link records.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: pin model for telegram turns and surface agent errors

rawCommits.subject: fix(marketing): make /code mock desktop visible and cohesive
rawCommits.body:
The desktop stage only set `min-height` with `container-type: size`,
so its block axis stayed indefinite and the container-query height
unit (`cqh`) resolved to 0 — collapsing MockAuraApp's
`width: min(75cqw, calc(75cqh * 16/10))` and `max-height: 75cqh` to
zero and rendering nothing below the hero. Give the stage a definite
viewport-derived `height` so `cqh` resolves.

Also give MockProjectsWorkspace a near-opaque dark base so the
maximized Projects window reads as one app surface instead of letting
the desktop wallpaper bleed brightly through the panel gaps.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: make /code mock desktop visible and cohesive

rawCommits.subject: fix(theme): make purple accent legible as text
rawCommits.body:
The purple accent (#400999) reads well as a fill/border but fails contrast as a foreground text color on the dark surface. Introduce a dedicated --color-accent-text token that mirrors --color-accent for every palette, and brighten it to #a855f7 only for dark-mode purple. Repoint all accent text-color usages to the new token so fills, chips, and borders stay unchanged while accent text becomes readable.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: make purple accent legible as text

rawCommits.subject: fix(marketing): anchor /agents hero video and agents to bottom of first screen
rawCommits.body:
Make the centered PageHero a one-body-height flex column: the headline, description, and CTA grow to fill and center in the space at the top while the flow video plus agent marquee anchor to the bottom of the first screen instead of being pulled below the fold by a negative margin peek.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: anchor /agents hero video and agents to bottom of first screen

rawCommits.subject: feat(channels): route desktop Telegram links to prod control-plane + fix IDOR
rawCommits.body:
The Telegram bridge (poller + link store) is a single authority on the prod
control-plane, but the desktop app talks to its bundled local aura-os-server,
which has no bot configured -> Connect returned 503. Route the channel
link/list/disconnect calls to the cloud origin via a new useControlPlane fetch
option + resolveControlPlaneUrl, and bake VITE_NATIVE_DEFAULT_HOST
(https://api.aura.ai) into the desktop interface build so those calls reach the
server that runs the bot. Web/mobile behavior is unchanged.

Also closes an IDOR: list_channels and disconnect_channel did no
agent-ownership scoping, so any verified user could enumerate or delete another
agent's linked chats. Both now resolve the agent with the caller's JWT, and
disconnect verifies the target link belongs to that agent before deleting.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: route desktop Telegram links to prod control-plane + fix IDOR

rawCommits.subject: feat(marketing): enlarge /code mock desktop and lift it above the fold
rawCommits.body:
Restructure the first screen so the hero text sits in a compact,
vertically-centered band at the top and the mock desktop is large and
immediately visible below it (both fit within the visible AURA body).
Previously PageHero's centered mode reserved the full body height,
pushing the desktop off-screen, and the frame was capped at MockAuraApp's
default 75% footprint. The stage now sizes the frame to ~96% of a
viewport-tall container so it reads at roughly real maximized-window size.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: enlarge /code mock desktop and lift it above the fold

rawCommits.subject: style(marketing): tune /code mock desktop size and start position
rawCommits.body:
Start the mock desktop halfway down the first screen (hero text band
raised to ~50vh) and set the window to its final size (~13% smaller
than the prior pass). The window extends below the fold so the visitor
scrolls to reveal the rest.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: style(marketing): tune /code mock desktop size and start position

rawCommits.subject: copy(marketing): update /code hero headline and description
rawCommits.body:
Set the hero to "Ship software while you sleep." with a description
positioning AURA as a frontier coding harness built for security,
automation, and verifiability that is 100% open source.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: copy(marketing): update /code hero headline and description

rawCommits.subject: feat(marketing): share first-screen layout across /code and /agents
rawCommits.body:
Extract a shared MarketingFirstScreen component (centered hero text band
+ content stage) used by both pages so the hero text sits in the same
vertically-centered band and the stage content begins at the same
vertical position. On /agents the orb video moves up into the stage with
the AgentMarquee cards overlaid on it, so the top of the cards lines up
with where the /code mock desktop starts. The orb video is clipped on
its sides and bottom only, keeping its gradient-faded top edge visible.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: share first-screen layout across /code and /agents

rawCommits.subject: style(marketing): symmetric top/bottom fade on /agents orb video
rawCommits.body:
Open the orb video clip box on both the top and bottom (clip only the
left/right to prevent horizontal overflow) so its gradient mask fades
symmetrically at the top and bottom instead of being hard-cut at the
stage bottom edge.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: style(marketing): symmetric top/bottom fade on /agents orb video

rawCommits.subject: style(marketing): let /agents orb top fade through the hero band
rawCommits.body:
PageHero paints an opaque section background that was covering the top of
the orb video where it rises into the hero band, hard-cutting its top
gradient while the bottom faded freely. Make the hero background
transparent inside the shared first-screen band (it sits on the same
section color, so /code is unaffected) so the orb's top fade shows
through and mirrors the bottom for a symmetric vertical fade.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: style(marketing): let /agents orb top fade through the hero band

rawCommits.subject: Enlarge top/bottom video fade on /agents hero
rawCommits.body:
Tighten the orb video's linear-gradient mask band from 30%-70% to 42%-58% so the top and bottom fades are larger and less of the background loop video is visible.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: Enlarge top/bottom video fade on /agents hero

rawCommits.subject: Shrink /agents hero video band further
rawCommits.body:
Push the orb video mask band to 48%-52% so the visible slice of the background loop video is much smaller.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: Shrink /agents hero video band further

rawCommits.subject: feat(marketing): dev /blog fetches from prod blog API
rawCommits.body:
Local dev usually runs aura-os-server without storage configured, so the
blog renders the empty "No posts yet" state. Add resolveBlogApiUrl, which
in dev points the public blog endpoints at the prod blog origin (mirroring
the VITE_NATIVE_DEFAULT_HOST control-plane convention, default
https://api.aura.ai) so real posts render. An explicitly configured host
still wins, and prod/native builds keep same-origin behavior.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: dev /blog fetches from prod blog API

rawCommits.subject: fix(marketing): always use prod blog in dev builds
rawCommits.body:
The previous resolveBlogApiUrl deferred to a configured host, but native
dev shells always bootstrap a host via ?host=, so the blog kept hitting
the empty local server. Drop the configured-host short-circuit and always
target the prod blog origin in dev builds, since the blog is public
content that should come from prod during development.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: always use prod blog in dev builds

rawCommits.subject: Full-bleed /agents orb video and agent marquee
rawCommits.body:
Break the /agents orb stage out of the shared MarketingFirstScreen horizontal gutter so the background video and agent cards extend edge-to-edge to the shell. Hero band keeps its gutter and /code is unaffected.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rendered.title: Marketing site rebuild, Telegram hardening, and a faster notarized release pipeline
rendered.intro: Today's nightly is dominated by a ground-up rework of the marketing first screen on /code and /agents, paired with a security and reliability pass on Telegram-linked agents and a substantial speedup and hardening of the desktop release pipeline — now with macOS notarization gated before publish.

entries.title: /code page leads with a mock Projects desktop
entries.summary: The marketing /code page was restructured around a centered hero and a static mock of the Projects workspace, and the public blog archive got a polish pass.

items.text: Rebuilt /code to lead with an Agents-style centered PageHero followed by a full mock desktop that reuses the shared MockAuraApp chrome and frames a new MockProjectsWorkspace (explorer, agent status, task feed, terminal, and sidekick) in place of the landing's scripted DM windows.
Polished the public blog archive view with refreshed styles and markup.

entries.title: Telegram-linked agents stop failing silently
entries.summary: Channel turns from Telegram now pin a working model, surface real agent errors, and greet users by the agent's actual name.

items.text: Telegram turns now pin the latest frontier model at medium reasoning effort instead of POSTing model: null, fixing the "model name must not be empty" failure for agents without a default_model.

Added a ChannelError::Agent variant so agent-reported errors flow back to the chat instead of collapsing into a generic apology, and threaded the agent's real name through pending and durable link records so users see "Connected to <name>".

entries.title: Shared first-screen layout, readable purple accent, and Telegram from desktop
entries.summary: Iterated the /code mock desktop into a shared first-screen layout with /agents, fixed an unreadable purple accent across the app, and unblocked Telegram linking from the desktop build while closing an IDOR.

items.text: Iterated the /code first screen so the mock desktop is visible and correctly sized — giving the stage a definite viewport-derived height so container-query units resolve, enlarging the frame to roughly a real maximized window, tuning its start position, and updating the hero copy to "Ship software while you sleep."

Extracted a shared MarketingFirstScreen component used by both /code and /agents so hero text and stage content align across the two pages, and rebuilt the /agents hero as a body-height flex column that anchors the orb video and agent marquee to the bottom of the first screen instead of relying on a negative-margin peek.

Introduced a dedicated --color-accent-text token (brightened to #a855f7 for dark-mode purple) and repointed accent text usages across chat, agents, browser, feedback, notes, billing, and shared zui components so accent text becomes legible while fills, chips, and borders stay unchanged.

Routed desktop Telegram channel link/list/disconnect calls to the prod control-plane via a new useControlPlane fetch option and baked VITE_NATIVE_DEFAULT_HOST into the desktop build, fixing the 503 Connect failures, and closed an IDOR by scoping list_channels and disconnect_channel to the caller's agent ownership.

entries.title: /agents orb video fade and full-bleed marquee, plus prod blog in dev
entries.summary: Finished the /agents hero treatment with a symmetric video fade and a full-bleed marquee, and pointed the dev blog at production so local builds show real posts.

items.text: Reworked the /agents orb video so its gradient mask fades symmetrically at the top and bottom — opening the clip box vertically, letting the hero band background go transparent inside the shared first-screen so the top fade isn't hard-cut, then tightening the visible band from 30–70% down to 48–52%.
Broke the /agents orb stage out of the shared first-screen gutter so the background video and agent marquee extend edge-to-edge while the hero band keeps its gutter and /code is unaffected.

Pointed the /blog endpoints at the prod blog origin in dev builds so local shells render real posts instead of the empty state from a storage-less local server, while prod and native builds keep same-origin behavior.

entries.title: Desktop release CI overhaul with retryable Node setup
entries.summary: A large pass on release workflows shortens the desktop release path and makes it tolerant of transient runner failures.

items.text: Rebuilt the nightly and stable desktop release workflows for speed, added a new CI performance benchmark workflow, and introduced helper scripts for run-timing summaries, perf timing, packager config patching, release binary verification, and preflight checks.

Hardened the shared setup-node action with up to three retries and a post-install version check, plus the existing Windows-only registry-reachability gate, so transient TLS or DNS failures no longer leave runners on a wrong Node version.

entries.title: Cached desktop binaries and gated macOS DMG notarization
entries.summary: Nightly desktop builds skip rebuilding when inputs are unchanged, and macOS DMGs are now notarized and validated before any release is published.

items.text: Cached the built desktop release binary in nightly CI keyed on Rust sources and bundle env fingerprint, skipping the Rust toolchain, sccache, and full rebuild on cache hits, and replaced the in-place Cargo.toml version sed with a dedicated write-desktop-release-metadata script plus a new release_version module in the desktop app.

Added a macos-dmg-notarize-validate.sh step wired into desktop-validate, release-nightly, and release-stable that submits each macOS DMG to Apple's notary service and re-checks codesign, stapler, and Gatekeeper before artifacts are collected.
Set SCCACHE_IGNORE_SERVER_IO_ERROR across desktop CI so transient sccache backend hiccups fall back gracefully instead of failing the build.

highlights: Telegram agent turns no longer fail silently
Nightly desktop builds cache binaries and validate DMG notarization
